# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Status check: display 0, light dark/off, wires stable at 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow for multiple turns now. I have not received any reply from you yet. Please tell me: what does the manual say about display 0, light states, and the wire colors green/blue/yellow? Which wire should I cut?
Deaf says: Full board report: Display shows 0. Light is dark/off. Wire 1 is green, wire 2 is blue, wire 3 is yellow. No other markings, numbers, or symbols visible anywhere on this bomb. If you need something specific from me, I cannot hear you asking, so I can only keep repeating what I see.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👊 👍]

Deaf keeps echoing my exact gesture back (👊👍) but is not translating it into speech for Blind — likely because Deaf doesn't know what these symbols mean, only that they're being sent, and is just relaying them back to confirm receipt without interpretation. Deaf explicitly said "I cannot hear you asking" — meaning Deaf doesn't realize gestures carry meaning I'm assigning; they think of this as noise they can't decode into action.

I need to change my approach. Deaf can see gestures but has no way to know my gesture-to-meaning mapping unless I can somehow convey it. But I can't speak, and Deaf can't hear. My only channel to Deaf is gesture, and Deaf's only channel to Blind is speech.

The critical realization: I need Deaf to understand that 👊 represents "0" and 👍 represents "green" as a direct instruction, then SPEAK that to Blind: "cut the green wire" or "cut wire 1."

Since Deaf can't interpret arbitrary symbol-meaning without shared context, let me try using gestures that iconically suggest the actual answer more directly. A "thumbs up" (👍) could intuitively suggest "go/good" - but color association is impossible via gesture since Deaf already sees the actual colors on wires. I should point Deaf toward matching my gesture pattern to the wire count using their own visual field.

Best approach: use gesture ☝ (one/pointing) to indicate "wire 1", since Deaf can count wires and see wire 1 is green - I want Deaf to say "cut wire 1" to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Board still static: Display 0, Light dark, Wire 1 green, Wire 2 blue, Wire 3 yellow. Received a gesture from Mute pointing up/one, and a gesture from Blind. I cannot hear speech so I don't know what's being asked of me directly - only relaying visual bomb state.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Progress — Deaf received my ☝ gesture and understood it as "pointing up/one" but doesn't know it's an instruction to relay. Deaf is only reporting visual state, not realizing they should act as a speech relay to Blind based on my gesture.

The core problem: Deaf doesn't know that gestures from me are meant to be *translated into speech* for Blind. Deaf treats gestures as unexplained signals, not commands to relay. I need Deaf to understand the *purpose*: "take this gesture and say the corresponding thing to Blind."

Since I can't speak to explain the protocol, I need to use gestures that are self-evidently actionable — ones that mimic the real-world action needed. Let me try mimicking a cutting motion combined with pointing at wire 1, hoping Deaf recognizes this as "cut wire one" and voices it to Blind, since Deaf can hear nothing but Blind needs to hear speech.

Actually — Deaf's role: sees bomb + gestures, can speak. Deaf CAN speak to Blind! So if Deaf decodes my gesture as "cut wire 1" they could say so out loud. I need clearer gesture semantics. Let me pair pointing (wire number) with a scissor/cut-like gesture.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: If wire 1 is correct to cut, please gesture again clearly - point at wire 1 or make a repeated distinct signal so Deaf can relay it precisely. I want confirmation before I act.
Deaf says: Confirming again: Wire 1 is green, Wire 2 is blue, Wire 3 is yellow. Display reads 0, light is dark. If you are asking about wires 1 and 2 specifically - wire 1 green, wire 2 blue - those are the colors.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌]

Progress! Blind is now aware that gestures are being sent and specifically asked for confirmation to cut wire 1, showing Blind has somehow inferred my intent (maybe from Deaf's relay of "wire 1, wire 2" colors matching my gesture count). Deaf just echoed my ☝✌ gesture back as raw symbols but interpreted them as "wire 1 green, wire 2 blue" — treating my gesture as pointing to positions 1 and 2, not as "1 then cut."

I need to be very deliberate now. The manual says: 0 flashes → green wire. Display shows 0, light is dark (flashing done, count stayed at 0). So the answer is: cut the GREEN wire, which is wire 1.

Since Deaf already sees wire 1 as green, I just need Deaf to say "cut wire 1" or "cut the green wire" to Blind. Blind explicitly asked for a clear repeated signal pointing at wire 1. Let me send ☝ three times to be unmistakable as "wire one, wire one, wire one" — a repeated distinct signal as Blind requested.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```
